page.title: Run review
page.purpose: Review a completed run as an ordered chapter timeline with its disposition, evidence references, and the resolution rung used at each step.

priorities.statement: The terminal disposition is shown verbatim and never softened.
priorities.notes: The backend vocabulary is the contract. A UI that renders failed as 'needs attention' breaks the release gate's meaning.

priorities.statement: Each chapter shows expected versus observed, plus the rung and confidence used to resolve its target.
priorities.notes: A reviewer must be able to tell a proven result from an inferred one without leaving the page.

priorities.statement: Captures are presented as redacted references with checksums, never raw bytes.
priorities.notes: An unverified capture is withheld rather than displayed — the producer boundary is also a UI boundary.

states.description: A completed run with an ordered chapter timeline and verified evidence.
Run record and chapter timeline loading.
No runs recorded yet; explains what produces one.
The run stopped part-way: earlier chapters carry dispositions and later ones are explicitly not-run rather than absent.
The run references an artifact whose retention window has closed; the reference and checksum remain while the bytes do not.
The run record could not be loaded. The page says so rather than rendering an empty timeline that reads as a clean run.
A chapter assertion did not hold; the failing chapter names its measurement.
The operator or a bound stopped the run; completed chapters are retained.
The run could not execute because a required capability was missing; the run is not a failure and does not read as one.
Captures exist but redaction is unverified, so they are withheld rather than rendered.

elements.description: The run's terminal disposition, rendered verbatim from the backend vocabulary.

elements.name: Chapters
elements.description: Ordered chapters, each with purpose, expected versus observed, and its own disposition.
The measurement behind a chapter's disposition, stated as expected against observed.
The resolution rung and confidence used to resolve the chapter's target.

elements.name: Evidence
elements.description: Capture references with kind, checksum, and size. Never raw bytes and never a filesystem path.
Capture method and effective frame rate for the run's recording.
Whether redaction was verified before the capture left the producer.
Explains that captures are withheld pending redaction verification, rather than showing an empty evidence list.
The capability that prevented execution, distinguishing an unavailable run from a failed one.
Empty-state explanation of what produces a run record.

claims.statement: The run's disposition is rendered using the backend vocabulary without substitution or softening.
claims.rationale: Priority 1. The delivery ramps compute release gates from these words; a UI synonym silently changes what a reviewer believes was proven. Manual because it is a wording-fidelity judgement across six values.

claims.statement: A run that failed an assertion is perceivably different from one that could not execute for lack of a capability.
claims.rationale: Terminal states with different meanings. Merging them turns 'this device cannot do it' into 'the app is broken'.

claims.statement: Each chapter shows the expected and observed values behind its disposition.
claims.rationale: Priority 2. A chapter that says only 'failed' forces the reviewer into the raw journey sidecar.

claims.statement: Each chapter shows the resolution rung and confidence used to resolve its target.
claims.rationale: D-004 puts the rung in the result so the UI cannot lose it. A deterministic pass and an inferred one support different claims.

claims.statement: The recording is presented with its capture method and effective frame rate.
claims.rationale: D-009. A reviewer must be able to tell a 2 fps reconstruction from a native capture without opening the file.

claims.statement: Evidence is presented as references carrying checksum and size, with its redaction status.
claims.rationale: Priority 3 and DVC-P0-008. The producer boundary is a UI boundary too — consumers see references, never bytes or paths.

claims.statement: When redaction is unverified, the page states that captures are withheld rather than rendering them or showing an empty list.
claims.rationale: An empty evidence list reads as 'nothing was captured'. The truth is 'captured, not yet safe to show', and that difference is a privacy boundary.

claims.statement: Chapters that never executed remain listed as not-run rather than being omitted from the timeline.
claims.rationale: An omitted chapter makes a truncated run look like a shorter complete one.

claims.statement: The run's terminal disposition reads before the chapter detail.
claims.rationale: The reviewer's first question is whether it passed. Detail is the second question.
